pr_title: Add node check to vSphere cloud provider
pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?
/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:
At KCM startup, vSphere cloud provider builds a cache from `NodeAdded()` events from an informer. But these events are asynchronous, the cloud provider may need information from the cache earlier, for example when detaching a volume from a node at KCM startup. If a node is missing in the cache, the cloud provider treats such a detach as successful, which is wrong. Such a volume will be attached to the node forever.

To prevent this issue:

1. Try `nodeLister` from the informer before declaring a node as not found. A/D controller starts after its node informer has been synced.

2. Read API server before declaring a node as not found. To be 100% sure a node has been really deleted and the informer does not have stale data.

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:
<!--
*Automatically closes linked issue when PR is merged.
Usage: `Fixes #<issue number>`, or `Fixes (paste link of issue)`.
_If PR is about `failing-tests or flakes`, please post the related issues/tests in a comment and do not use `Fixes`_*
-->
Fixes #117091

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

Since vSphere CSI migration is GA, the vSphere cloud provider is used only to detach volumes from 1.25 and older nodes (unless the migration is disabled). 

I've tested this with hacked errors in the cloud provider to fail Detach requests + restarted KCM - with this PR, I can see  in logs:

```
Node jsafrane-8pmvh-worker-xlb2s found in vSphere cloud provider node informer
```

Which means the node is not in NodeManager's cache and the old cloud provider would treat all volumes used by this node as detached. With this PR, the cloud provider actually detaches volumes from the node.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?
<!--
If no, just write "NONE" in the release-note block below.

-->
```release-note
Fixed vSphere cloud provider not to skip detach volumes from nodes at kube-controller-startup.
```

issue_context.title: In-tree vSphere volumes are not detached after KCM restart
issue_context.body:
### What happened?

I am enabling CSI migration on a vSphere cluster. A node was fully drained, all its Pods are deleted, but just before KCM detaches in-tree vSphere volume volumes from it, KCM restarts. A new KCM starts, sees attached volumes in `node.status.volumesAttached` that are not needed by any Pod on the node and calls vSphere in-tree volume plugin `Detach()`.

The in-tree vSphere volume plugin + cloud provider marks the volume as detached right away, without reaching to vCenter API. The volume remains attached forever.

I don't think it's related to CSI migration, IMO a regular node drain + KCM restart at the same time can cause the same issue.

KCM logs:

```
I0404 14:58:42.423920       1 operation_generator.go:1637] Verified volume is safe to detach for volume "nil" (UniqueName: "kubernetes.io/vsphere-volume/[WorkloadDatastore] 8b577f5f-ea23-1e5e-bac9-0693938623e5/_029e/_0040/7f718f6c06a84cff86e254dfcd150be1.vmdk") on node "jsafrane-rdpmz-worker-ps6qk" 
I0404 14:58:42.423986       1 nodemanager.go:359] No VM found for node "jsafrane-rdpmz-worker-ps6qk". Initiating rediscovery.
E0404 14:58:42.434007       1 nodemanager.go:362] Error "No VM found" node info for node "jsafrane-rdpmz-worker-ps6qk" not found
I0404 14:58:42.434051       1 nodemanager.go:395] node info for node "jsafrane-rdpmz-worker-ps6qk" not found
E0404 14:58:42.434074       1 vsphere.go:651] Cannot find node "jsafrane-rdpmz-worker-ps6qk" in cache. Node not found!!!
E0404 14:58:42.434101       1 attacher.go:287] Error checking if volume ("[WorkloadDatastore] 8b577f5f-ea23-1e5e-bac9-0693938623e5/_029e/_0040/7f718f6c06a84cff86e254dfcd150be1.vmdk") is already attached to current node ("jsafrane-rdpmz-worker-ps6qk"). Will continue and try detach anyway. err=No VM found
I0404 14:58:42.434114       1 nodemanager.go:359] No VM found for node "jsafrane-rdpmz-worker-ps6qk". Initiating rediscovery.
E0404 14:58:42.434127       1 nodemanager.go:362] Error "No VM found" node info for node "jsafrane-rdpmz-worker-ps6qk" not found
I0404 14:58:42.434130       1 nodemanager.go:395] node info for node "jsafrane-rdpmz-worker-ps6qk" not found
E0404 14:58:42.434133       1 vsphere.go:651] Cannot find node "jsafrane-rdpmz-worker-ps6qk" in cache. Node not found!!!
I0404 14:58:42.434138       1 vsphere.go:1020] Node "jsafrane-rdpmz-worker-ps6qk" does not exist, disk [WorkloadDatastore] 8b577f5f-ea23-1e5e-bac9-0693938623e5/_029e/_0040/7f718f6c06a84cff86e254dfcd150be1.vmdk is already detached from node.
I0404 14:58:42.434160       1 operation_generator.go:513] DetachVolume.Detach succeeded for volume "nil" (UniqueName: "kubernetes.io/vsphere-volume/[WorkloadDatastore] 8b577f5f-ea23-1e5e-bac9-0693938623e5/_029e/_0040/7f718f6c06a84cff86e254dfcd150be1.vmdk") on node "jsafrane-rdpmz-worker-ps6qk" 
```

The in-tree cloud provider has a [node informer](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/legacy-cloud-providers/vsphere/vsphere.go#L1547) and [maintains a list of nodes](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/d89d5ab2680bc74fe4487ad71e514f4e0812d9ce/staging/src/k8s.io/legacy-cloud-providers/vsphere/nodemanager.go#L290) from it. It apparently has not processed all nodes at the time A/D controller tries to detach the node.

### What did you expect to happen?

The in-tree vSphere volume plugin + cloud provider detaches the volume in vCenter.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

That's really tricky, it's very hard / impossible to reproduce on a real cluster. I had to inject errors to Detach() in-tree volume call, so they fail until KCM is restarted. Newly started KCM would detach the volume just fine (no error would be injected there), but marks the volume as detached right away.

### Anything else we need to know?

For the record (and search-ability), the CSI driver that tries to attach the volume to another node complains either:

```
Warning  FailedAttachVolume  26m (x10 over 31m)   attachdetach-controller  AttachVolume.Attach failed for volume "pvc-24d840d4-89eb-4619-945d-fce26be85015" : rpc error: code = Internal desc = failed to set keepAfterDeleteVm control flag for VolumeID "76f9905e-22ff-443d-bf8e-1af270ab5b46"
```

Or:

```
LocalizedMessage: (string) (len=32) \"The resource 'volume' is in use.\"\n})\n". opId: "1bb54dd7"
```

cc @xing-yang @jingxu97 @msau42 @gnufied @divyenpatel

It could be somewhat related to https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/vsphere-csi-driver/issues/2165, however, not all cases of https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/vsphere-csi-driver/issues/2165 can be related to KCM restart. As I mentioned above, it's very hard/impossible to synchronize KCM restart with draining a node in a real cluster.

comments:
Tried just moving a Pod between nodes without CSI migration involved + restarting KCM when the volume is still attached to the old node. In-tree volume plugin on the new node says:

```
  Warning  FailedAttachVolume  66s (x3 over 67s)  attachdetach-controller  AttachVolume.Attach failed for volume "pvc-24d840d4-89eb-4619-945d-fce26be85015" : No VM found
  Warning  FailedAttachVolume  8s (x2 over 38s)   attachdetach-controller  AttachVolume.Attach failed for volume "pvc-24d840d4-89eb-4619-945d-fce26be85015" : Failed to add disk scsi0:1.
```
What CSI driver version and K8s version are you testing with?
Kubernetes is 1.25 and CSI driver is 2.7, still, I think it's not releated to the CSI driver, it's KCM who marks the in-tree volume as detached due to not populated node cache.

I found an easier way how to reproduce this without extra code in KCM:

1. Run a StatefulSet with 1 Pod that uses 1 PVC.
2. Cordon the node where the Pod runs.
3. Scale down kube-controller-manager to zero (not really possible for me) *or* kill all kube-controller-manager Pods. This will cause new KCM processes to wait for leader election. In my env. this gives me ~30 seconds for the next step.
4.  Delete the Pod. A new one will be scheduled on a different node (because the current node is cordoned) + there is no KCM running at this time that would detach the volume from the old node.
5. New KCM wins its leader election, sees a volume attached to a node where it is not needed -> it calls `Detach()` of the volume plugin. VSphere cloud provider does not have its caches populated yet (= this bug) -> the volume is not detached, but `Detach()` returns success.
